title: Cataloguing and Classification
topics: Purpose and forms of the catalogue

items.q: Original cataloguing may be defined as
o: a set of marks in which each added symbol narrows the meaning of the one before
the preparation of a record from the item itself rather than from a copy
the area that shows whether an item is a first or a later version of the same work
a term taken from an approved list to stand for one idea in an index
items.s: Original cataloguing: the preparation of a record from the item itself rather than from a copy. The other options describe Edition statement, Descriptor, Hierarchical notation.

items.q: The statement “the name or word placed at the top of an entry to fix its place in the file” describes which of the following?
o: Heading
Corporate body
See also reference
Uniform title
items.s: Heading is the name or word placed at the top of an entry to fix its place in the file.

items.q: Which of the following best describes RDA?
o: the standard number, now of thirteen digits, that identifies a published book uniquely
a protocol that lets one system search and copy records held in another
the standard issued in 2010 to replace the older code and to suit linked data environments
a table of common facets, such as form or place, that may be added to any number
items.s: RDA: the standard issued in 2010 to replace the older code and to suit linked data environments. The other options describe ISBN, Z39.50, Standard subdivisions.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Notation?
o: a term not used for indexing but entered in a list as a pointer to another
a set of marks in which each added symbol narrows the meaning of the one before
the symbols, usually figures or letters, that stand for a class in a scheme
the broad divisions running from zero hundred to nine hundred in the Dewey scheme
items.s: Notation: the symbols, usually figures or letters, that stand for a class in a scheme. The other options describe Ten main classes, Hierarchical notation, Non-descriptor.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Table of precedence?
o: marks in which each added figure multiplies tenfold the detail that is expressed
the part of a shelf address that stands for the subject of an item
a ruling on which of two conflicting numbers is to be preferred
the preparation of a record from the item itself rather than from a copy
items.s: Table of precedence: a ruling on which of two conflicting numbers is to be preferred. The other options describe Original cataloguing, Decimal notation, Class mark.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines UDC.
o: marks that mix letters and figures in a single shelf address
the scheme first published in 1876 that divides all knowledge into ten main groups
the scheme developed from Dewey, adding symbols for combining numbers and common aspects
the international framework that fixes the order and punctuation of the areas of a description
items.s: UDC: the scheme developed from Dewey, adding symbols for combining numbers and common aspects. The other options describe DDC, Alphanumeric notation, ISBD.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Access point?
o: the moving of stock from one scheme, or one edition, to another
the work of keeping the forms of names and subjects consistent throughout a file
a direction from a form of name not used to the one that is used
a name, word or number under which a record may be sought in a file
items.s: Access point: a name, word or number under which a record may be sought in a file. The other options describe Authority control, Reclassification, See reference.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Imprint?
o: the full record of an item, filed under the heading chosen as its principal approach
the closeness of a chosen term to the exact matter of the item in hand
the details of where, by whom and when an item was issued
the fixed order in which the aspects of a subject are strung together to make a number
items.s: Imprint: the details of where, by whom and when an item was issued. The other options describe Main entry, Specificity, Facet formula.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Authority control?
o: a controlled set of terms linked by broader, narrower and related relationships
the work of keeping the forms of names and subjects consistent throughout a file
a system meant to cover every field of knowledge rather than one discipline
a record of what a collection contains that gives only brief details of each item
items.s: Authority control: the work of keeping the forms of names and subjects consistent throughout a file. The other options describe Finding list, Thesaurus, Universal scheme.

items.q: Which term is described by “a secondary heading that gives another route to the same record”?
o: Added entry
Corporate body
Heading
Authority file
items.s: Added entry is a secondary heading that gives another route to the same record.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines LCSH?
o: the large approved list maintained by the Library of Congress for use in its catalogues
the placing of items into groups according to their likeness, and the arranging of those groups in a helpful order
the checking of items against the order they should occupy, to find misfiles
a system that builds a number by combining separate aspects of a subject
items.s: LCSH: the large approved list maintained by the Library of Congress for use in its catalogues. The other options describe Classification, Faceted scheme, Shelf reading.

items.q: Which term is described by “the scheme first published in 1876 that divides all knowledge into ten main groups”?
o: DDC
Standard subdivisions
Manual
Relative index
items.s: DDC is the scheme first published in 1876 that divides all knowledge into ten main groups.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Facet formula?
o: the fixed order in which the aspects of a subject are strung together to make a number
the full record of an item, filed under the heading chosen as its principal approach
the set of marks placed on an item to fix its position on the shelf
a list of the approved forms of names and subjects, with the variants rejected
items.s: Facet formula: the fixed order in which the aspects of a subject are strung together to make a number. The other options describe Main entry, Authority file, Call number.

items.q: Which term is described by “a shorter approved vocabulary of subject terms intended for small and medium sized libraries”?
o: Non-descriptor
Sears List
Pre-coordination
Descriptor
items.s: Sears List is a shorter approved vocabulary of subject terms intended for small and medium sized libraries.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Retrospective conversion.
o: the transfer of an old card file into machine readable form
a table of common facets, such as form or place, that may be added to any number
the scheme first published in 1876 that divides all knowledge into ten main groups
the five fundamental categories of personality, matter, energy, space and time
items.s: Retrospective conversion: the transfer of an old card file into machine readable form. The other options describe PMEST, Standard subdivisions, DDC.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Card catalogue?
o: a cabinet of drawers in which each item is represented by a set of typed slips
a system meant to cover every field of knowledge rather than one discipline
the standard form of a name used to bring together versions of the same work
an organisation or group, such as a ministry or a society, treated as the maker of a work
items.s: Card catalogue: a cabinet of drawers in which each item is represented by a set of typed slips. The other options describe Universal scheme, Corporate body, Uniform title.

a protocol that lets one system search and copy records held in another

marks in which each added figure multiplies tenfold the detail that is expressed
the standard form of a name used to bring together versions of the same work

items.s: Decimal notation: marks in which each added figure multiplies tenfold the detail that is expressed. The other options describe Added entry, Uniform title, Stocktaking.

the area that shows whether an item is a first or a later version of the same work
the part of a record that sets out the title, responsibility, issue and extent of an item
a table of common facets, such as form or place, that may be added to any number
items.s: Close classification: the assignment of the most detailed number that the schedule allows. The other options describe Bibliographic description, Edition statement, Standard subdivisions.

the assignment of the most detailed number that the schedule allows
a set of marks in which each added symbol narrows the meaning of the one before

Pre-coordination
Sears List
Post-coordination

o: ISBD
Bibliographic description
Call number
AACR2

items.q: Fixed field may be defined as
o: the part of the address that separates items of like subject, often by author
the part of a machine readable record that holds coded data of set length
a completely rewritten set of numbers that replaces an older one in a new edition
the area that shows whether an item is a first or a later version of the same work
items.s: Fixed field: the part of a machine readable record that holds coded data of set length. The other options describe Book number, Edition statement, Phoenix schedule.

items.q: Which term is described by “the scheme developed from Dewey, adding symbols for combining numbers and common aspects”?

UDC
Close classification
Universal scheme

a system meant to cover every field of knowledge rather than one discipline
the count of the pages or volumes that make up an item
a ruling on which of two conflicting numbers is to be preferred
